question: to the Commission Galato Alexandraki (ECR) Subject:

According to the Commission, the AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026. The rules on high-risk systems set out in Annex III will apply from 2 December 2027 and from 2 August 2028 for the respective systems that have been integrated into products. Clear information is needed on the aspects that are already in place to protect citizens and what will come into force later on. It is therefore considered necessary to provide practical guidance for the human review of adverse decisions. The human review should be carried out by trained officials who are best placed to reject an algorithmic recommendation. Before public authorities use such systems, I would suggest establishing common standards for independent checks and publishing a brief risk assessment that is easy to understand, with personal data protection. Small and medium-sized businesses need easy-to-use compliance tools. Likewise, providers must provide sufficient documentation and not pass their responsibilities on to small users in a non-transparent way. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
When will uniform practical guidance be given on reporting, human review and explaining decisions, depending on the applicable regime?
How are citizens affected by the systems in Annex III protected during the transition period?
What tools will be given to SMEs to exercise compliance and check the documentation of their suppliers?
